\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{बेहद} (behad)}{बेहद (behad)}]{\hi{बेहद} (behad) — extremely, beyond measure}

\label{lesson:HI-C387-behad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for stubbornness, then the Hindi for eligible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बेहद}}
\textbf{\hi{बेहद}} — \emph{behad} — \textquotedblleft{}extremely, beyond measure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{आज} \hi{भी} \hi{बेहद} \hi{गर्मी} \hi{रही} \hi{तो} \hi{स्कूल} \hi{बंद} \hi{रहेंगे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āj bhī behad garmī rahī to skūl band raheṅge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it is extremely hot again today, the schools will stay shut.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{बेहद}} (\emph{behad}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{behadd}, \textquotedblleft{}without limit\textquotedblright{}. It joins Persian \emph{be-}, \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{}, to Arabic \emph{ḥadd}, \textquotedblleft{}a limit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āj bhī behad garmī rahī to skūl band raheṅge.} — If it is extremely hot again today, the schools will stay shut.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for stubbornness, then the Hindi for eligible, then say \emph{behad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{बेहद} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Extremely, beyond measure\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{अत्यंत} (atyant)}{अत्यंत (atyant)}]{\hi{अत्यंत} (atyant) — extremely (formal)}

\label{lesson:HI-C387-atyant}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for eligible, then the Hindi for extremely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{अत्यंत}}
\textbf{\hi{अत्यंत}} — \emph{atyant} — \textquotedblleft{}extremely (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{रोगी} \hi{की} \hi{हालत} \hi{अत्यंत} \hi{गंभीर} \hi{होगी} \hi{तो} \hi{उसे} \hi{अस्पताल} \hi{ले} \hi{जाना} \hi{पड़ेगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar rogī kī hālat atyant gambhīr hogī to use aspatāl le jānā paṛegā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the patient's condition is extremely serious, he will have to be taken to hospital.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{अत्यंत}} (\emph{atyant}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{atyanta}, \textquotedblleft{}excessive, very great\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atyant}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atyant}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar rogī kī hālat atyant gambhīr hogī to use aspatāl le jānā paṛegā.} — If the patient's condition is extremely serious, he will have to be taken to hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for eligible, then the Hindi for extremely, then say \emph{atyant} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{अत्यंत} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Extremely (formal)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{ज़रा} (zarā)}{ज़रा (zarā)}]{\hi{ज़रा} (zarā) — a little, a bit}

\label{lesson:HI-C387-zara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for extremely, then the Hindi for extremely (formal).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ज़रा}}
\textbf{\hi{ज़रा}} — \emph{zarā} — \textquotedblleft{}a little, a bit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{ज़रा} \hi{धीरे} \hi{बोलो}, \hi{वरना} \hi{बच्चा} \hi{जाग} \hi{जाएगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zarā dhīre bolo, varnā baccā jāg jāegā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Speak a little more quietly, or the baby will wake up.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{ज़रा}} (\emph{zarā}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{dharra}, \textquotedblleft{}a speck, an atom\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian. Persian says \emph{zarra}; the Hindi sense is a little.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zarā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zarā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zarā dhīre bolo, varnā baccā jāg jāegā.} — Speak a little more quietly, or the baby will wake up.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for extremely, then the Hindi for extremely (formal), then say \emph{zarā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{ज़रा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A little, a bit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{ख़ूब} (khūb)}{ख़ूब (khūb)}]{\hi{ख़ूब} (khūb) — plenty, a lot}

\label{lesson:HI-C387-khub}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for extremely (formal), then the Hindi for a bit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ख़ूब}}
\textbf{\hi{ख़ूब}} — \emph{khūb} — \textquotedblleft{}plenty, a lot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{ख़ूब} \hi{बारिश} \hi{होगी} \hi{तो} \hi{फ़सल} \hi{अच्छी} \hi{होगी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar khūb bāriś hogī to fasal acchī hogī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there is plenty of rain, the harvest will be good.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{ख़ूब}} (\emph{khūb}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{khūb}, \textquotedblleft{}good, fine\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khūb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar khūb bāriś hogī to fasal acchī hogī.} — If there is plenty of rain, the harvest will be good.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for extremely (formal), then the Hindi for a bit, then say \emph{khūb} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{ज़बरदस्त} (zabardast)}{ज़बरदस्त (zabardast)}]{\hi{ज़बरदस्त} (zabardast) — tremendous, powerful}

\label{lesson:HI-C387-zabardast}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a bit, then the Hindi for plenty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ज़बरदस्त}}
\textbf{\hi{ज़बरदस्त}} — \emph{zabardast} — \textquotedblleft{}tremendous, powerful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{हमारी} \hi{टीम} \hi{जीत} \hi{गई} \hi{तो} \hi{गाँव} \hi{में} \hi{ज़बरदस्त} \hi{दावत} \hi{होगी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar hamārī ṭīm jīt gaī to gā̃v meṁ zabardast dāvat hogī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If our team wins, there will be a tremendous feast in the village.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{ज़बरदस्त}} (\emph{zabardast}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{zabardast}, \textquotedblleft{}strong-handed, superior\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a bit, then the Hindi for plenty, then say \emph{zabardast} again
\end{itemize}
